title: Avoca Alternatives for Service Businesses
description: Compare Off The Clock AI, Sameday AI, ServiceTitan Voice Agent and Jobber Receptionist as alternatives to Avoca for service businesses.
intro: Compare Off The Clock AI, Sameday AI, ServiceTitan Voice Agent and Jobber Receptionist as alternatives to Avoca for service businesses.
verdict: Evaluate Off The Clock when pricing the actual job is the priority. Compare Sameday for a broader phone operation, or a native Jobber/ServiceTitan option when keeping your current platform is the main requirement.
reason: Avoca is more than an AI voice on the phone. Its material describes call scoring and a Human in the Loop program staffed by Avoca-trained CSRs. A useful alternative must be judged against the modules and coverage you actually need. [[avoca-coach]] [[avoca-human]]

First decide what is failing in your present process. Is it unanswered inquiries, appointment handling, calls that need a person, or owners still having to price every project? These problems can require different products even when their feature lists overlap.

The reviewed Avoca pages are demo-led and do not establish a numerical subscription price. Obtain a written offer instead of filling that gap with a third-party estimate. Ask whether coaching, campaigns, human handling and integrations are part of the same purchase. [[avoca-product]]
choices: When the pricing conversation keeps returning to you

Off The Clock’s reason to be on the shortlist is QuoteDone. Use the evaluation to distinguish a complete owner-priced job from a booked estimate or a lead that still needs pricing. The correct review path is also an outcome worth testing.
When phones and follow-up are a broader requirement

Compare the tasks your office does around the call, not just the voice quality. Walk through a returning customer, an appointment change and follow-up ownership. Define exactly which jobs the AI may complete.
When ServiceTitan should remain the center
Use the native option as a baseline against an added front-office vendor. Check what the agent can do with your booking rules and what a supervisor can inspect afterward.
When a Jobber-native answering feature is enough
For an existing Jobber business, start with the actual incremental feature and bill. Do not buy a broader contact-center package simply because the original shortlist contained one.

scenario.title: The test: a handoff that does not restart the conversation
scenario.text: Ask an ordinary service question, explain a complication, then request a person. Evaluate the handoff as a complete experience. A transfer button is not the same thing as the right person receiving the right job details.
checks: Who receives the call: your team, a contracted external team or another queue?
Which scope, customer context and unanswered questions survive the transfer?
When nobody is available, what reaches the owner and what does the customer hear?

questions: Who supplies the human escalation team, during which hours, and at what cost?
Which reporting and coaching modules are included rather than optional?
Can your team see and correct an incorrect outcome classification?
decision: Keep Avoca in consideration when coaching, escalation and connected front-office operations are the real requirement. Choose a narrower product deliberately when those extras are not needed. For an owner whose unfinished task is the quote, evaluate Off The Clock against that task directly.
faqs: Yes. Its Human in the Loop program uses Avoca-trained CSRs. Confirm whether that program and its coverage are included in your proposal. [[avoca-human]]
Its official integration page describes direct booking and customer-context writeback while the office continues using ServiceTitan. [[avoca-servicetitan]]
